claims.text: The initial feedstock is FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy-alloy powder with a particle size of 15–45 μm.
The 15–45 μm FeCoNiCrAl feedstock was previously used with the HVAF-M3 torch.
Reducing the HVAF-i7 nozzle-to-substrate distance will increase particle impact velocity.
Spray distances of 300–350 mm were identified as favorable for MCrAlY coatings.
Higher particle velocity will improve deposition efficiency.
Improved deposition efficiency will produce thicker FeCoNiCrAl bond coats.
Increasing particle velocity through spray-distance optimization will not sacrifice oxidation resistance.
Enhanced particle kinetic energy produces better flattening and adhesion upon impact.
Better particle flattening and adhesion improve inter-particle bonding and coating buildup.
A shorter spray distance enhances particle melting and deformation upon impact.
Improved particle contact and energy transfer enable more efficient buildup of coating layers.
The proposed intervention will maintain the microstructural integrity and low oxidation associated with the M3-deposited 15–45 μm feedstock.
Optimized spray distance will yield a significantly thicker and well-adherent bond coat than the baseline HVAF-i7 process.
The optimized coating will exhibit minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
HVAF-M3 deposition of 15–45 μm feedstock yields high-quality coatings.
Using the same feedstock-related parameters with HVAF-i7 yields acceptable coating quality but inadequate thickness.
The intervention is expected to remain effective when coating internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
The intervention is expected to remain effective under high-temperature service conditions.
Excessive spray-distance reduction may overheat particles or the substrate.
Particle or substrate overheating may increase oxidation or cause microstructural degradation.
